answer: In a Sybil-resistant mechanism, agents create unique digital "gardens" containing cryptographically secure identifiers. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to control a large number of distinct "river" paths, connecting these gardens to the network. However, verification protocols can detect and discard "hollow" gardens lacking legitimate agent activity, forcing an attacker to expend substantial computational resources to maintain convincing fake identities, thereby raising the cost of Sybil attacks.
